Subject: Embeddings integration & migration — post-call next steps

Thanks again for the call this morning — really appreciate the time, Samir and Priya.

Quick recap + proposed next steps based on what we discussed:

Recap
- Current state: you have ~6M documents indexed with OldVector (production), using 1024-d vectors for semantic search.
- Goal: reduce query latency/cost and centralize model/version control with predictable latency for reranking flows.
- Constraints: minimal downtime for search, ability to backfill embeddings in batches, and compatibility with existing doc IDs.

Key technical items we agreed to follow up on
1) Vector dimensions and model recommendations
   - We'll validate tradeoffs between 768 vs 1536 dims for your corpora. Shorter dims are cheaper and faster; higher dims can improve recall for long-form content.
2) Batching and import strategy
   - Plan for chunked bulk-export from OldVector -> staged import into Redwood. We'll provide a sample bulk importer script.
3) Normalization
   - Recommendation: L2-normalize and store unit vectors for cosine similarity; supply guidance if you want to keep raw (unnormalized) vectors for other metrics.
4) Auth/SDK setup
   - We'll share Python/Node SDK snippets and a short checklist for API keys + service-role auth for backfills.
5) Routing & fallbacks
   - Suggest a canary: route 5% of traffic to Redwood embeddings + reranker, keep fallback to OldVector until quality gates pass.
6) Reranker approach
   - Two-step: 1) dense retrieval with embeddings + approximate kNN, 2) cross-encoder rerank for final top-K. We'll help size the cross-encoder capacity.

Attachments I’m including: redwood-embeddings-migration-checklist.xlsx (migration checklist and roles), and a short import checklist. Please also find a placeholder file acme-vector-specs.csv if you want to share an export of your current vector metadata.

Next steps (proposed)
- Dev & SE deep-dive (60m): technical migration plan, sample scripts, and SLA expectations — propose Tue May 26 10:00am PT / 1:00pm ET.
- Provide your sample export (ID+text+vector) or a small sample (1k rows) to validate normalization and dimensionality.
- We’ll run a quick embed comparison on a 1k sample and share precision@10 for 768 vs 1536.

Action items for you
- Samir/Priya: share 1k sample export or grant a temporary read-only export link.
- Internal: Dev, can you prepare the sample importer + SDK snippets?

If that all looks good I’ll send a calendar invite for Tue.

Thanks Marissa — included some technical notes below that I’ll bring to the deep-dive. Quoted your email for context.

> Recap
> - Current state: you have ~6M documents indexed with OldVector (production), using 1024-d vectors for semantic search.

Notes / recommendations (short):
- Vector dims: if your dataset is mostly short QA and product docs, 768/fast open models (e.g. open-embedding-1) often gives similar downstream recall vs 1024 at ~60% lower cost. For long-form enterprise docs, we should run a quick A/B on 768 vs 1536.
- Normalization: store unit vectors (L2 norm) to use cosine via dot-product. We recommend normalizing at write time and storing as float16 (if your storage supports) to save space.
- Batching for import: use 10k-chunk batches for the initial backfill; concurrent workers of 4-8 per region depending on your throughput. Redwood supports a /v1/embeddings/import endpoint for multipart uploads — I’ll attach the sample importer script.
- ID mapping: keep your existing doc_id as external_id in Redwood so you can switch read paths without remapping in search app.
- Tokenization/model drift: since different embedding models use different tokenizers, similarity space can shift — do a small 1k sample test to measure retrieval quality.
- Reranker sizing: expect cross-encoder rerank to add ~50-200ms per query depending on model; we can auto-scale this in Dedicated if you need SLA-backed latency.

Sample Python snippet (pseudo):

import redwood_sdk
client = redwood_sdk.Client(api_key="REDACTED")

# normalize and upload in batches
def normalize(vec):
    norm = sum(x*x for x in vec)**0.5
    return [x / norm for x in vec]

for chunk in chunked(rows, 10000):
    payload = [{"id": r["doc_id"], "vector": normalize(r["vector"]), "metadata": r["metadata"]} for r in chunk]
    client.embeddings.import_batch(payload)

I’ll attach the sample importer and a short checklist (permissions, service account, rate limits). I can also prepare a small script to convert OldVector export -> Redwood import format.

I’ll join Tue 26 10am PT.

Perfect — thanks for the export, Samir.

Answers to your quick clarifications:
- Ballpark storage: 6M vectors -> at 768 dims float32 = ~18.4 GB (6e6 * 768 * 4 bytes) ; at 1536 dims = ~36.9 GB. If you use float16 you can halve that. I’ll include a short cost worksheet in the meeting.
- Backfill approach: yes — we recommend write-to-new-index + alias swap (zero-downtime). Redwood supports alias rollovers and atomic switches; we’ll include a step-by-step in the checklist.
- Auth checklist: service-role API key with restricted scopes + IP allowlist or VPC peering for bulk backfills. Dev attached a checklist and sample IAM policy in the drive link.

I’ve sent the calendar invite for Tue May 26 10:00am PT. Agenda: migration plan, sample importer walkthrough, auth checklist, and quick embed A/B test plan. Please upload the 1k sample to the Drive link before the call if possible.

See you on Tue —
Marissa
